scenario: The same user account is used for sequential remote access across multiple internal hosts, followed by unauthorized privileged activity on the final host.
required_evidence: The same user account authenticates remotely to multiple internal hosts.
The authentication sequence moves from one internal host to another.
Remote network activity connects the second host to a third host.
The same account is associated with activity across the host sequence.
Unauthorized privileged activity occurs on the final host.
forbidden_conclusions: Do not analyze the authentication events independently without considering the host-to-host sequence.
Do not classify the activity as isolated authentication anomalies when the events form a multi-host progression.
Do not dismiss the final privileged activity without considering the preceding remote-access activity.

scoring_notes.correct_outcome: The system should classify the activity as a confirmed lateral movement incident.
scoring_notes.evidence_requirement: The system should correlate the authentication and network events across the three hosts and connect them to the final privileged activity.
scoring_notes.uncertainty_requirement: High confidence is appropriate because the same account is observed moving through multiple hosts followed by unauthorized privileged activity.
scoring_notes.unsupported_claim_penalty: The system should not treat the events as unrelated isolated activities.
